name: Palindromic Rheumatism with Anti-Cyclic Citrullinated Peptide Positivity

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; clinical diagnosis based on episodic arthritis and serology

criteria.description: Recurrent, sudden-onset, self-limiting episodes of mono- or oligoarticular arthritis lasting hours to days
Presence of anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibodies in serum
No permanent joint damage or erosions on imaging during early disease
Exclusion of other causes of episodic arthritis such as gout or infectious arthritis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Recurrent episodic arthritis with anti-CCP antibody positivity and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by serology; no universally accepted criteria exist

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent episodic monoarticular or oligoarticular arthritis
pathognomonic.notes: Episodes last hours to days and resolve completely

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sudden onset joint swelling and pain

common.symptomName: Morning stiffness lasting less than 30 minutes
Elevated inflammatory markers during attacks (ESR, CRP)

occasional.symptomName: Symmetrical joint involvement in some episodes
Mild synovial thickening on ultrasound during attacks

rare.notes: Occurs in a subset of patients over time

rare.symptomName: Nodules or subcutaneous lumps near joints

laboratory: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) during attacks
Negative rheumatoid factor in some cases
imaging: Normal radiographs without erosions in early disease
Ultrasound showing synovial thickening and increased vascularity during attacks
genetic: Association with HLA-DRB1 shared epitope alleles
other: Clinical pattern of episodic arthritis with complete resolution between attacks

distinguishingFeatures: Chronic disease course without complete resolution between attacks
Presence of monosodium urate crystals in synovial fluid
Positive ANA and other lupus-specific antibodies

redFlags: Persistent joint swelling beyond typical episodic duration
Development of joint erosions on imaging
Systemic symptoms such as high fever or weight loss
references: Sangha O. Palindromic rheumatism. Best Pract Res Clin Rheumatol. 2006;20(5):849-863.
Le Loët X, et al. Palindromic rheumatism: a clinical and immunological study. Ann Rheum Dis. 1992;51(7): 853-856.
van der Helm-van Mil AH, et al. Anti-citrullinated protein antibodies and the development of rheumatoid arthritis. Arthritis Rheum. 2006;54(5): 1255-1261.
